answer: To defend against Sybil attacks, the protocol deploys a hierarchical topology audit where each agent must prove localized computational routing depth. An automated falcon probe verifies route latency across an open network meadow, ensuring no single entity simulates diverse peers. If an attacker creates hundreds of pseudonymous agents, their traffic bottlenecks into a narrow canyon of shared network hardware and synchronized clock drift. Colluding clusters face automated collateral slashing, imposing an escalating capital cost of thousands of dollars per fake identity.
